{{Short description|Canonical commutation or anticommutation relations}}
In [[mathematics]] and [[physics]] '''CCR algebras''' (after [[canonical commutation relation]]s) and '''CAR algebras''' (after canonical anticommutation relations) arise from the [[quantum mechanics|quantum mechanical]] study of [[boson]]s and [[fermion]]s, respectively. They play a prominent role in [[quantum statistical mechanics]]<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Bratteli |first1=Ola |title=Operator Algebras and Quantum Statistical Mechanics: v.2 |last2=Robinson |first2=Derek W. |publisher=Springer, 2nd ed |year=1997 |isbn=978-3-540-61443-2 |author-link=Ola Bratteli |author-link2=Derek W. Robinson}}</ref> and [[quantum field theory]].

==CCR and CAR as *-algebras==
{{Citation needed|reason=This section contains definitions without sourcing. Please provide a reliable academic reference.|date=July 2025}}

Let <math>V</math> be a [[real number|real]] [[vector space]] equipped with a [[Algebraic curve#Singularities|nonsingular]] real [[Skew-symmetric matrix#Skew-symmetric and alternating forms|antisymmetric]] [[bilinear form]] <math>(\cdot,\cdot)</math> (i.e. a [[symplectic vector space]]). The [[unital algebra|unital]] [[*-algebra]] generated by elements of <math>V</math> subject to the relations

:<math>fg-gf=i(f,g) \, </math>
:<math> f^*=f, \, </math>

for any <math>f,~g</math> in <math>V</math> is called the '''canonical commutation relations (CCR) algebra'''. The uniqueness of the representations of this algebra when <math>V</math> is [[finite dimensional]] is discussed in the [[Stone–von Neumann theorem]].

If <math>V</math> is equipped with a [[Algebraic curve#Singularities|nonsingular]] real [[symmetric bilinear form]] <math>(\cdot,\cdot)</math> instead, the unital *-algebra generated by the elements of <math>V</math> subject to the relations

:<math>fg+gf=(f,g), \,</math>
:<math> f^*=f, \,</math>
for any <math>f,~g</math> in <math>V</math> is called the '''canonical anticommutation relations (CAR) algebra'''.

==The C*-algebra of CCR==

There is a distinct, but closely related meaning of CCR algebra, called the CCR C*-algebra. Let <math>H</math> be a real symplectic vector space with nonsingular symplectic form <math>(\cdot,\cdot)</math>. In the theory of [[operator algebra]]s, the CCR algebra over <math>H</math> is the unital [[C*-algebra]] generated by elements <math> \{W(f):~f\in H\}</math> subject to
:<math> W(f)W(g)=e^{-i(f,g)}W(f+g), \,</math>
:<math> W(f)^*=W(-f). \,</math>
These are called the Weyl form of the canonical commutation relations and, in particular, they imply that each <math>W(f)</math> is [[unitary operator|unitary]] and <math>W(0)=1</math>. It is well known that the CCR algebra is a simple (unless the symplectic form is degenerate) non-separable algebra and is unique up to isomorphism.<ref>{{Cite book
 | last=Petz | first=Denes
 | title=An Invitation to the Algebra of Canonical Commutation Relations
 | publisher=Leuven University Press
 | year=1990
 | isbn=978-90-6186-360-1
 | url=http://www.math.bme.hu/~petz/ccr.html
 }}</ref>

When <math>H</math> is a complex [[Hilbert space]] and <math>(\cdot,\cdot)</math> is given by the imaginary part of the inner-product, the CCR algebra is [[representation theory|faithfully represented]] on the [[fock space|symmetric Fock space]] over <math>H</math> by setting
: <math> W(f)\left(1,g,\frac{g^{\otimes 2}}{2!},\frac{g^{\otimes 3}}{3!},\ldots\right)= e^{-\frac{1}{2}\|f\|^2-\langle f,g\rangle }\left(1,f+g,\frac{(f+g)^{\otimes 2}}{2!}, \frac{(f+g)^{\otimes 3}}{3!}, \ldots\right), </math>
for any <math>f,g \in H</math>. The field operators <math>B(f)</math> are defined for each <math> f\in H</math> as the [[Stone's theorem on one-parameter unitary groups|generator]] of the one-parameter unitary group <math>(W(tf))_{t\in\mathbb{R}}</math> on the symmetric Fock space. These are [[self-adjoint operator|self-adjoint]] [[unbounded operator]]s, however they formally satisfy
:<math> B(f)B(g)-B(g)B(f) = 2i\operatorname{Im}\langle f,g\rangle. </math>
As the assignment <math>f\mapsto B(f)</math> is real-linear, so the operators <math>B(f)</math> define a CCR algebra over <math>(H,2\operatorname{Im}\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle)</math> in the sense of [[#CCR and CAR as *-algebras|Section 1]].

==The C*-algebra of CAR==

Let <math>H</math> be a Hilbert space. In the theory of operator algebras the CAR algebra is the unique [[complete metric space|C*-completion]] of the complex unital *-algebra generated by elements <math>\{b(f),b^*(f):~f\in H\}</math> subject to the relations
:<math>b(f)b^*(g)+b^*(g)b(f)=\langle f,g\rangle, \,</math>
:<math>b(f)b(g)+b(g)b(f)=0, \,</math>
:<math>\lambda b^*(f)=b^*(\lambda f), \,</math>
:<math>b(f)^*=b^*(f), \, </math>
for any <math>f,g\in H</math>, <math>\lambda\in\mathbb{C}</math>.
When <math>H</math> is separable the CAR algebra is an [[Approximately finite dimensional C*-algebra|AF algebra]] and in the special case <math>H</math> is infinite dimensional it is often written as <math>{M_{2^\infty}(\mathbb{C})}</math>.<ref>{{cite book
| last1 = Evans | first1 = David E. | author-link = David E. Evans
|last2=Kawahigashi |first2=Yasuyuki | author-link2 = Yasuyuki Kawahigashi 
| title = Quantum Symmetries in Operator Algebras
| publisher = Oxford University Press
| year = 1998
| isbn = 978-0-19-851175-5
}}.</ref>

Let <math>F_a(H)</math> be the [[Fock space|antisymmetric Fock space]] over <math>H</math> and let <math>P_a</math> be the  orthogonal projection onto antisymmetric vectors:
:<math>P_a: \bigoplus_{n=0}^\infty H^{\otimes n} \to F_a(H). \, </math>
The CAR algebra is faithfully represented on <math>F_a(H)</math> by setting
:<math> b^*(f)P_a(g_1\otimes g_2\otimes\cdots\otimes g_n)=\sqrt{n+1}P_a(f\otimes g_1\otimes g_2\otimes\cdots\otimes g_n) \, </math>
for all <math> f,g_1,\ldots,g_n\in H</math> and <math>n\in\mathbb{N}</math>. The fact that these form a C*-algebra is due to the fact that creation and annihilation operators on antisymmetric Fock space are bona-fide [[bounded operator]]s. Moreover, the field operators <math>B(f):=b^*(f)+b(f)</math> satisfy
:<math> B(f)B(g)+B(g)B(f)=2\mathrm{Re}\langle f,g\rangle, \, </math>
giving the relationship with [[#CCR and CAR as *-algebras|Section 1]].

==Superalgebra generalization==
Let <math>V</math> be a real <math>\mathbb{Z}_2</math>-[[graded vector space]] equipped with a nonsingular antisymmetric bilinear superform <math>(\cdot,\cdot)</math> (i.e. <math>(g,f)=-(-1)^{|f||g|}(f,g) </math> ) such that <math>(f,g)</math> is real if either <math>f</math> or <math>g</math> is an even element and [[imaginary number|imaginary]] if both of them are odd. The unital *-algebra generated by the elements of <math>V</math> subject to the relations

:<math>fg-(-1)^{|f||g|}gf=i(f,g) \,</math>
:<math>f^*=f,~g^*=g\,</math>

for any two pure elements <math>f,~g</math> in <math>V</math> is the obvious [[superalgebra]] generalization which unifies CCRs with CARs: if all pure elements are even, one obtains a CCR, while if all pure elements are odd, one obtains a CAR.

In mathematics, the abstract structure of the CCR and CAR algebras, over any field, not just the complex numbers, is studied by the name of [[Weyl algebra|Weyl]] and [[Clifford algebra]]s, where many significant results have accrued. One of these is that the [[graded algebra|graded]] generalizations of [[Weyl algebra|Weyl]] and [[Clifford algebra|Clifford]] algebras allow the basis-free formulation of the canonical commutation and anticommutation relations in terms of a symplectic and a symmetric non-degenerate bilinear form. In addition, the binary elements in this graded Weyl algebra give a basis-free version of the commutation relations of the [[symplectic Lie algebra|symplectic]] and [[indefinite orthogonal group|indefinite orthogonal Lie algebras]].<ref>{{cite journal|author=Roger Howe|title=Remarks on Classical Invariant Theory|journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society|volume=313|year=1989|issue=2|pages=539–570|jstor=2001418|doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-1989-0986027-X|doi-access=free}}</ref>
